messages:
Maya R.: quick follow-up from RFC: need a tiny emergency fallback policy runtime can evaluate under 400ms. goal: stop noisy premature rollbacks.

Owen T.: current issue: transient p99 spikes cause immediate route-to-baseline, which hurts quality for some routes. propose two-tier decision: runtime uses short-window dominance check for latency (fast), control-plane uses weighted scoring for stable actions.

Selina H.: agree. runtime actions list: reduce-batch, fallback-quantized, route-to-baseline. each action has priority and min_dwell_s.

Maya R.: hysteresis: require either N consecutive breaches OR sustained average > threshold for T seconds. also min_samples to avoid noise.

infra-bot: probe: route=/embed p99=860ms target=400ms samples=150 eval_delta=+2.1%

Owen T.: implementation sketch: latency_score = clamp((p99 - target)/target,0,1); quality_score = clamp((baseline_eval - current_eval)/baseline_eval,0,1). runtime evaluates if max(latency_score * w_l, quality_score * w_q) > threshold.

Selina H.: control-plane will run weighted-sum over 5-15m windows and can revoke/relax policy. runtime always emits decision_event to control-plane append-only stream.

Maya R.: alerts: P0 if route-to-baseline occurs without prior control-plane inform; P1 for 3 soft-degrades in 30m. add sim tests for latency-only, quality-only, combined.

Owen T.: action items: Owen -> tiny runtime evaluator + README blurb (next Tue). Selina -> policy schema PR (fields: policy_id, strategy, weights, threshold, min_samples, windows, actions, cool_down) by Mon. Maya -> add sim harness tickets.

Selina H.: noted, will keep defaults conservative (quality-first).
